title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2→3 bridge: Orthodox consent — regenerating Grace of Christ not to all but to God’s peculiar own; Propos. 3 opens on mere mercy without prior person-difference
pass_a_gloss: Ye see now from the consent of the Orthodox that the Grace of Christ properly so called, that is, regenerating and saving, is not given unto all, but unto certain persons whom God peculiarly claims as his own. There remains the last proposition, which most contains the cause, and which among all the Orthodox was no less in confession than the two former. That Grace of Christ which consists in the infusion of faith, charity, and of all gifts necessary unto infallibly effecting salvation, (that is, which heals the soul, which gives to will the good and to accomplish it) is not given unto men from antecedent regard unto some better operations or dispositions of the receivers, nor denied unto others from antecedent regard unto their worse operations or dispositions as non-receivers, but from the mere will of God showing mercy on whom he wills, and not showing mercy on whom he wills not, without any respect unto a previous discrimination of persons.
pass_b_english: From Orthodox consent you see: the Grace of Christ properly so called—regenerating and saving—is not given to all, but to certain persons God peculiarly claims as his. The last proposition remains, which most holds the cause, and which all the Orthodox confessed no less than the two before. That Grace of Christ which consists in infusing faith, charity, and every gift needed to effect salvation infallibly—that is, which heals the soul and gives to will and finish the good—is not given from prior regard to some better acts or dispositions in the receivers, nor denied from prior regard to worse acts or dispositions in non-receivers, but from God’s mere will of mercy on whom he wills and non-mercy on whom he wills not, with no respect to a prior difference of persons.
source_text: Videtis jam ex consensu Orthodoxorum, Gratiam Christi proprie dictam, hoc est, regenerantem et salvantem, non dari omnibus, sed certis personis quas pro suis Deus peculiariter vendicat. Restat ultima propositio, quae causam maxime continet, quaeque apud omnes Orthodoxos non minus in confesso fuit, quam duae priores. Illa gratia Christi quae constat infusione fidei, charitatis, atque omnium donorum ad salutem infallibiliter efficiendam necessariorum, (hoc est, quae sanat animam, quae dat bonum velle et perficere) non datur hominibus ex antecedaneo intuitu ad meliores aliquas operationes aut dispositiones accipientium, neque negatur aliis ex antecedaneo intuitu ad pejores illorum operationes aut dispositiones non accipientium, sed ex mera Dei voluntate miserentis cujus vult, et cujus non vult non miserentis, absque omni respectu ad praevium discrimen personarum.
